scope: Original transfer-ring record building, lane draining, register reading and submission paths; full reached/final machine/RAM/FPU/banks/MACH/MACL/GBR, timer, software graphics/transfer registers, ordered native boundaries, store queues and captured packets. Independent complete ring-builder RAM/stack footprint, wrap/alignment/record/start-register/interrupt-mask checks and drain semantics. Six actual frame-finalizer -> submission sequences reach the unresolved completion wait.
limitations: The seven DMA command words are bounded host storage only; no asynchronous hardware transfer, interrupt delivery, completion or pixels are fabricated.

Research retry/wait bounds stop with -4 before the second continued branch test; builds without SA_BOUND_RETAIL_STALLS retain original unbounded loops. Typed host failures are not complete hardware exceptions.

Submission remains partial at its real callback/interrupt-dependent wait paths, with zero parent recovery credit. Initial runtime tables, native no-op/unknown callbacks and finite timer samples are explicit fixtures. Complete direct submission returns exercise explicit skip-submit state; starting a real transfer still reaches a pending completion wait.

The six producer/consumer sequences carry RAM and CPU/FPU state. The producer makes no bus/clock effects, so the reinitialized backend has identical empty state; the finalizer does not alter the extra integer/MACH/MACL/GBR state. This is not a general persistent interrupt/device scheduler.
Inherited privileged bank-1/FD=0, immutable code/literals, valid distinct stack/data and MMU-off domains apply. Gameplay, natural boot/scheduling and all requested ports/settings remain incomplete.
